verdict.summary: Any organization owner can add an OAuth app under Organization settings > OAuth Apps and start authorizing users of other organizations right away, with no review step documented. The catches are that you can't fetch a project's database password through the Management API, and the OAuth app's rate limit is shared by everyone calling through it.

evidence.label: inferred
evidence.note: Add the app in org settings, copy the client ID and secret, and run the code + PKCE flow against api.supabase.com.

timeToProd.assumes: A self-published OAuth app that manages projects or runs SQL via the Management API. A Partner Catalog listing is optional and only adds visibility (Supabase's partner review is a separate track).

evidence.label: inferred
evidence.note: Neither the integration guide nor the publish page mentions a review. The Partner Catalog docs list listing criteria but don't link them to OAuth access.

prerequisites.item: A Supabase account and an organization you can administer
prerequisites.why: OAuth apps are created from the organization's settings, on the OAuth Apps tab.

evidence.label: sourced
evidence.note: The docs don't say which org role is needed; owner/admin is our assumption.

prerequisites.item: An HTTPS redirect URI and a server that can keep the client secret
prerequisites.why: The token exchange authenticates with the client ID and secret through a Basic auth header.

prerequisites.item: A way to collect the user's database password if your agent needs direct Postgres access
prerequisites.why: The docs say you 'cannot retrieve the database password via the management API'.

scopeTiers.impact: Enough for an agent that inspects projects, branches, functions and logs. Scopes are fixed on the app, not per request.

evidence.label: tested
evidence.note: Scope strings from scopes_supported in api.supabase.com/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server on 2026-10-20.

scopeTiers.impact: database:write covers running SQL through the Management API. secrets:read returns project API keys. Powerful, but no extra review is documented.
Lets the agent create projects, deploy functions and manage branches. Creating projects can incur cost on the user's org.

steps.title: Sign in and pick the organization
steps.detail: Sign in to the Supabase dashboard and open the organization that will own the OAuth app.

steps.title: Choose the minimal scope set
steps.detail: Map the agent's features to Management API endpoints and pick read/write scopes. Changing scopes later forces existing users to re-authorize.

steps.title: Add the OAuth app
steps.detail: Organization settings > OAuth Apps > Add application. Enter name, website, redirect URIs and scopes, click Confirm, and copy the client ID and secret.

steps.title: Implement authorize + PKCE
steps.detail: Redirect to https://api.supabase.com/v1/oauth/authorize with client_id, redirect_uri, response_type=code, state, code_challenge (S256), and optionally organization_slug. Keep redirect_uri + state under 4 kB.

steps.title: Exchange the code and store tokens
steps.detail: POST https://api.supabase.com/v1/oauth/token (form-urlencoded, Basic auth) with grant_type=authorization_code, code, redirect_uri and code_verifier. Store access and refresh tokens; refresh with grant_type=refresh_token.

steps.title: Wire Management API calls with 429 handling
steps.detail: Use supabase-management-js or raw calls. Back off on 429; some endpoints are limited to 30 or 10 requests/min.

steps.title: Add the Connect Supabase button
steps.detail: Add a Connect Supabase button following Supabase's brand asset guidelines.

steps.title: Test with a second organization
steps.detail: Authorize from an account in a different org to confirm the app works for outside users and that the org picker appears.

steps.title: Optionally apply for a Partner Catalog listing
steps.detail: Apply to the Partners program for visibility. Listing criteria: business viability, no 'Supabase' in your name, your own Terms, Privacy and Acceptable Use policies, and long-term maintenance.

agentCanDo: Pick the minimal Management API scopes
Implement the authorize, PKCE, token and refresh flow
Build Management API calls with 429 backoff
Draft partner listing copy and policies if you want a listing
humanMustDo: Sign in and add the OAuth app in organization settings
Copy and store the client secret
Test authorization from a second organization
Ask users for their database password when direct Postgres access is needed

blockers.cause: The client_id is wrong or the app was deleted.
blockers.fix: Copy the client ID from Organization settings > OAuth Apps.

evidence.label: tested
evidence.note: Seen with a dummy UUID on 2026-10-20 (HTTP 422).

blockers.symptom: Agent can't connect to Postgres directly after OAuth
blockers.cause: The database password can't be retrieved via the Management API.
blockers.fix: Run SQL through the Management API with database:write, or prompt the user for the password.

blockers.symptom: Calls start returning 429 Too Many Requests at moderate traffic
blockers.cause: For OAuth apps, the rate limit applies to the app and is shared by everyone calling through it.
blockers.fix: Cache reads, queue writes, and back off until the window resets.

blockers.symptom: 403 or missing permission on an endpoint after adding a feature
blockers.cause: Scopes are set on the app and new scopes only apply after users re-authorize.
blockers.fix: Add the scope in the app settings and send existing users through the authorize flow again.

evidence.label: sourced
evidence.note: The exact status code is inferred.

blockers.symptom: Refresh fails or calls return 401 for a previously working user
blockers.cause: The user revoked access to your app.
blockers.fix: Handle 401 by sending the user back through authorization.

nuances.text: OAuth tokens are short-lived and tied to specific scopes. The docs don't give the access token lifetime.
Rate limit is 120 requests/min per user, per project or org, per endpoint, with some endpoints at 30 or 10/min. For OAuth apps the limit is shared by everyone calling through the app.
The scope query parameter is deprecated. Scopes come from the app config, and changing them forces existing users to re-authorize.
The live OAuth metadata advertises a dynamic client registration endpoint (/platform/oauth/apps/register) and a jwt-bearer grant, which the integration guide doesn't document.

evidence.label: tested
evidence.note: Observed on 2026-10-20. Likely used by MCP clients; we didn't call it.

nuances.text: The docs scope table also lists Auth, Domains, Rest and Secrets write scopes that don't appear in the live scopes_supported list, so the docs and live config may differ.
For single-user agents, scoped personal access tokens are an alternative to OAuth; the docs say 'Prefer scoped PATs' over legacy PATs.
